say.dc2a27b5c742.note: First words of the game. Low and close. A breath after 'burned low'; 'the ground is moving' plainly, not spooky.

say.3dcd3f3caa00.intent: tells the survivor the fire is no protection
say.3dcd3f3caa00.note: Matter-of-fact; the second sentence lands harder by being plainer.

say.2b72fa1dd85e.intent: shows the ambush before it springs
say.2b72fa1dd85e.note: Three images, each its own weight. A held beat before 'They were waiting', said colder and lower.

say.77eb67f9e183.note: Even through 'dead watchman', then the last sentence slower: it turns to look at you.

say.0663505a2971.intent: the first dead you killed was a child
say.0663505a2971.note: The narrator never shows a feeling: plain, the same pace throughout, and the facts do the grief. No catch before 'twelve at most'; 'and new boots' no softer than the rest. That restraint is the scene.

say.87080a48980a.intent: reads a dead man and his last words
say.87080a48980a.note: The book's three lines read as written words, each a little more unsettled than the last; 'singing in the water' nearly a whisper.

say.4e278cbc120f.intent: a dead man speaks to you alone
say.4e278cbc120f.note: The narrator's part only; the watchman says the quote.

segments.text: ...and for you alone, the dead man's jaw moves:
It shatters its own lamps when it charges. Make it charge.

say.1e2fc7986134.intent: the fight ends, something waits ahead
say.1e2fc7986134.note: Exhale on 'The dead go quiet.' Then hushed, drawn forward: water, and a cold blue light.

say.f1f67faea5fb.note: Deadpan on 'The graves are listening.' Not spooky; simply true.

say.f67dd9f6e97c.intent: the Warden is seen for the first time
say.f67dd9f6e97c.note: Half a whisper. Space after 'in the ford'. 'with a lamp in its fist' plain and heavy.

say.33579e176a7e.note: Breathing again after the fight. 'full of cold light' with quiet wonder.

say.4d8a46e7502e.intent: the quake stops; the way is north
say.4d8a46e7502e.note: 'For now.' on its own, dry. The road north plainly, a little warmer.

say.3eba0841cd10.note: The first warmth in the narrator's voice. 'then gold' opens up.

say.656db5d6ed09.intent: the ember fades and takes something of you with it
say.656db5d6ed09.note: The prologue's last word. Even and kind through the rules of it; then much quieter for the mother's face. 'not quite where you left it' almost tender, and wrong.

say.c4d495431666.intent: death will not take you yet
say.c4d495431666.note: Low, a little ominous, not triumphant.

say.8c1f7c369819.note: A list of sensations, unhurried. 'News travels fast here.' dry.

say.a49e30d2ba1e.note: Lift slightly on 'places the road forgets'.

say.6947705bd0e4.intent: a small human mark on the well
say.6947705bd0e4.note: Read 'M. plus J.' as letters: 'em and jay'.
say.6947705bd0e4.say: The water is a long way down, and clean. Somebody has scratched M and J into the stone.

say.8b004f74544d.note: 'turns sweetly' with a hint of relish; the ledger line dry.

say.ff981a5b72be.note: Quiet, careful, like a lockpick's breath.

say.a5b99f61e011.note: The note read gently, as written words: 'Keep the lights lit.' Then the initial: 'C.'
say.a5b99f61e011.say: Beside the old captain's stone, sunk in the nettles, a trunk the Watch forgot: ember shards, a purse, and a note. Keep the lights lit. C.

say.3ff82d4e2ac7.intent: the wolf cloak has damned you
say.3ff82d4e2ac7.note: Tighten on the second sentence: every wolf is on its feet.

say.3a93e764b57c.intent: the Pack knows what you did
say.3a93e764b57c.note: The second sentence a quiet reproach: Maeca warned you.

say.74fcfb5cdf24.intent: the Kerchiefs take you for a friend
say.74fcfb5cdf24.note: Tense first half, relaxed on 'go back to their dice'.

say.31fa91331b11.note: Build the size slowly. A dry little pause around 'probably', then 'dead' flat and doubtful.

say.b76e3053dc5f.note: The most important hush in Act 1. Each of 'slow, patient, enormous' its own breath. 'Not breathing.' then a long beat. 'Praying.' barely voiced.

say.0b5e75f9dfa0.intent: the caravan was robbed, not eaten
say.0b5e75f9dfa0.note: Deadpan on 'Wolves do not drive wagons.'

say.e6c4fb3a8998.note: Clipped observations, a beat before 'Under the seat'.

say.20dc615919d1.intent: the trail leads to the ravine

say.cfa493798ba7.note: Warm and soft; the only comfort in the wood.

say.8e845892b699.note: A list like a surgeon's; the last sentence slower and darker.

say.52d0f1dfa274.intent: a wolf dead of no wound

say.7197a1b189a3.note: Three senses, unhurried; 'a chapel lamp' with a faint wrongness.

say.84f6c2c74004.note: Clipped, observant. Lift on 'the drag-marks of lamps' (a clue).

say.769a1c759f88.note: Tight and fast. 'Run.' sharp but not shouted.

say.384c340b6b6d.note: 'like an eye opening' slower. 'The door is listening.' hushed.

say.9757e1dab88e.note: The last clause dry and ominous.

say.66cdbe61b828.note: The inscription read gravely as old words. 'all empty' quiet.
say.66cdbe61b828.say: Old-empire script over the door. Here the Seventh Legion buried what it could not burn. Below it, a sigil with seven notches, all empty.

say.99be1ad2c25a.note: 'It hums against your teeth.' close and physical.

segments.text: The skull turns, very slightly, toward you.
It was never locked from the outside.

say.6e1fab16785e.intent: someone went in and did not come out
say.6e1fab16785e.note: 'None coming away.' alone, ominous. The token a careful find.

say.b40ac14379d8.intent: a treasure where wolves go to die

say.1a95cdeef839.note: No sentiment; the nails are the detail.

say.75abd0854536.note: A small half-smile in the voice.

say.185a7c3f55e7.intent: Jory, freed, asks for his uncle

segments.text: Jory. Jory Coyle. Is my uncle... Is he...

say.f1bc8c3f22ed.note: Each stopping its own short sentence, settling.

say.a4755c96100b.note: Unflinching and quiet. 'Most of them do not crawl far.' almost gentle, which is worse.

say.26621b48a47e.note: Level, no relish. A breath before 'and then there is only the fire', said very low.

say.0622cbb5851c.note: Quick on the fire, softer on the glade.

say.005625eee2b8.note: Effort, then softer on the glade.

dlg.greymuzzle.first.0.note: A nature-documentary stillness. Long beat after 'for a long time'. The last image very quiet.

dlg.greymuzzle.show.0.note: Plain and close; 'and cannot' after a small beat. End on him waiting: an open question.

dlg.greymuzzle.ally.0.note: 'He is not coming.' alone. 'They are his answer.' warm and grave.

dlg.greymuzzle.again.0.intent: the Pack has turned its back

dlg.greymuzzle.again.2.note: A smile in the last clause.

dlg.tam.fetch.0.note: Wry on 'one of them is a fool'. 'He comes.' warm and short.

dlg.chid.relight.0.note: The words of the Order said with care. 'as if it had been waiting for it' with wonder. The kettle line with a smile.

dlg.maeca.blind.1.note: Close and unhurried, tasteful, no breathiness. The last image tender and a little wry.

dlg.sella.night.1.note: Fond and discreet. A smile at 'laughs at the last one' and 'nobody's business but yours'. 'She is dressed, and counting.' dry.

dlg.sella.free_night.1.note: Slower and softer than her paid night. 'which she has never done' a small revelation.
